summary: Marion L. Matics (1917–1998) worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He earned his PhD at Columbia University in 1960 under Horace L. Friess and Robert A. Fowkes, later teaching Oriental philosophy at Columbia and Brooklyn College.

Marion Meyer (born 1954) is a history and archaeology scholar. She studied at the University of Munich and earned her PhD from the University of Bonn (1984), later serving as Associate Professor at Bonn (1997–2003) and Full Professor at the University of Vienna (2003–2020).

Marion Rastelli is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed doctoral studies under Gerhard Oberhammer. She held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2000–2004, 2019–2022) and has lectured at the University of Vienna (attested 2020–2026).
Marius Zemp specializes in linguistics and Tibetology. He completed a Lizentiat at the University of Bern (1999–2014), where he subsequently served as a lecturer from 2020 to 2025.

Mark A. Nathan is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at UCLA in 2010 under Robert E. Buswell Jr., later holding posts as a visiting professor at Kangwon National University and lecturer at University at Buffalo (attested 2014).

Mark Allon is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Cambridge under K. R. Norman (~1990–1994) and served as Associate Professor at the University of Sydney beginning in 2002.

Mark Collins specialized in linguistics and Indology, earning a PhD from the University of Leipzig (1905–1907). He held professorships at Banaras Hindu University (1900–1904), Trinity College, Hartford (1908–1914), and the University of Madras (1914–1919), and worked at Visva-Bharati University (1922–1931).

Mark Condos is a historian of South Asia who completed his PhD at the University of Cambridge (2009–2013). He was an Early Career Research Fellow at Queen Mary University of London (2014) and became Senior Lecturer at King's College London in 2020.

Mark Csikszentmihalyi (born 1964) specializes in Sinology and philosophy. He was an Associate Professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1994–2007) before becoming a Professor at the University of California, Berkeley in 2010.

Mark D. Griffiths (born 1966) earned a BSc from the University of Bradford (~1984–1987) and a PhD from the University of Exeter (1988–1990). He held a lectureship at the University of Plymouth (1990–1995) and became Professor of Gambling Studies at Nottingham Trent University (1995–2025).

Mark Elliott is a scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. He served as a history professor at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1993–2003) and became Professor of Chinese and Inner Asian History at Harvard University in ~2003.

Mark Hale is a scholar in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. His academic posts include affiliations with Harvard University (attested 1987) and Concordia University (attested 1997).

Mark I. Wallace (born 1956) works in religious studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD in theology at the University of Chicago under Paul Ricœur (~1982–1986), taught at Georgia State University (~1987–1989), and became Professor of Religion at Swarthmore College in ~1989.

Mark Jan Dresden (1911–1986) was an Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological linguist. He earned his PhD at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda (~1937–1941) and served as Professor of Iranian Studies at the University of Pennsylvania from 1949 to 1980.

Mark Juergensmeyer (born 1940) specializes in religious studies and Indology. He earned a PhD in political science from UC Berkeley (1967–1974) and became Director of Global and International Studies and professor at UC Santa Barbara in 1993.

Mark L. Blum is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He held an associate professorship at the University at Albany, SUNY (attested 2004–2006) and serves as Professor and Shinjo Ito Distinguished Chair in Japanese Studies at UC Berkeley (attested 2026).

Mark McClish is an Indology and religious studies scholar who was a doctoral student of Patrick Olivelle. He served as Assistant Professor of Religion at Birmingham-Southern College (attested 2012–2015) and Director of Graduate Studies at Northwestern University (attested 2018–2020).

Mark McLaughlin is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He has held appointments at the College of William & Mary as Visiting Assistant Professor (attested 2017) and Senior Lecturer of South Asian Religions (attested 2021–2023).
Mark Owen is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies who completed his doctoral studies under supervisors Anna King and Elizabeth Stuart.
Mark Pedersen specializes in computational linguistics. He completed his PhD at the University of Queensland in 2001 and held a post at the same institution.
